text:
anya: Quick follow-up from the onboarding RFC — we need to lock the perf + compatibility contract for the adapter shim. I sketched a 3-stage gate (smoke -> perf sig -> full regression). Thoughts?

mario: 3-stage sounds right. we should define exact metrics for perf sig (p50/p95 latency, tokens/s, memory). also decide sample workloads.

sophie: Agree. Suggest we keep smoke very cheap: start up, forward pass for 8 typical inputs, and kv-cache sanity. Perf sig should use seq length distribution from telemetry.

kevin: We need explicit binary compatibility flags from adapters: supports_kv_cache, supports_batched_step, uses_cuda_extensions. Otherwise routing falls apart.

ravi: +1 on flags. Also include "max_context_tokens" and "quantized_variants" in metadata. We hit a hidden-size mismatch once because adapter omitted "kv_dtype".

anya: Good call. I'll add a minimal schema: {adapter_metadata: name, version, supports_kv_cache(bool), batched_step(bool), max_context(int), kv_dtype:string, quantized:list}. We'll keep it lightweight.

mario: For perf harness, propose this CLI: 
```
run_bench --model ./adapter --workload ./telemetry_sample.json --warmups 20 --iters 200 --out bench://results/123
```
bench-bot should capture and post results.

bench-bot: New bench run queued: results://bench/1765432100 (link: https://bench.redwood/reports/1765432100) :robot_face: 

sophie: On flakiness: we must use CI pinned infra to avoid noisy perf. Add a stability metric (stddev over 5 runs) and reject if >10%.

kevin: Tradeoff: stricter stability reduces throughput of onboarding. Maybe auto-retry up to 2 times, then escalate. Also we should allow a "canary" opt-in to bypass perf gate for dev experimentation.

ravi: For validation, include small functional evals: generation correctness on 50 golden prompts + token-level logprobs check for degenerated outputs. Keep seeds fixed.

anya: Summarized acceptance criteria for a model to pass onboarding: 
1) Smoke: starts, forward ok, metadata present.
2) Perf sig: p50 within X% of profile OR tokens/s above threshold; stability within limit.
3) Regression: nlg evals pass quality thresholds (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim).

I'll draft the exact numeric thresholds in a PR.

mario: Interface boundary question — should adapters expose a single unified call `generate(inputs, ctx)` or separate `encode`/`decode_step` hooks?

sophie: For runtime performance we want step-level access (decode_step) to reuse KV & custom kernels. But higher-level generate is easier for tests. So support both; tests use generate wrapper that calls decode_step under the hood.

kevin: Implementation note: adapter shim should expose both but mark generate as convenience. Router will prefer step-level when available. Document fallback behavior clearly.

ravi: Also add a small JSON contract test in PR that validates adapter metadata + example invocation: 
```json
{
  "name": "my-model",
  "supports_kv_cache": true,
  "batched_step": true,
  "max_context": 8192
}
```

anya: Next steps: I'll open a PR with the schema + bench CLI + the draft thresholds. @mario can you hook bench-bot to post a short summary in this thread when a run completes?

mario: Yep, I'll add a small webhook. bench-bot will post p50/p95, tokens/s, stddev and link. :thumbsup: 

sophie: Thanks — once PR is up I'll run a few model adapters through it and report flaky cases in a follow-up.

kevin: If we hit false positives from perf gate, let's add a human override path in Console. We should avoid long-blocking of customer onboarding.

anya: Agreed. I'll include an "override_reason" field in the onboarding record and a short audit trail.

bench-bot: Bench run completed: results://bench/1765432100 — p50=42ms p95=110ms tokens/s=850 stddev=4.2% link: https://bench.redwood/reports/1765432100

ravi: Looks within our tentative limits. I'll wait for the PR for exact thresholds then start the regression evals.

anya: Great. PR ETA EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone.
